ev.e03_fc_foundling.adopt.ok: The foundling was taken in, and the two of you lay in one cradle, head to head. Your father gave the little one a name and counted it among the household's fosterlings.
ev.e03_fc_foundling.neighbor: Take the baby to the neighbour
ev.e03_fc_foundling.neighbor.ok: The childless neighbour pressed the baby to her breast and burst into tears. She swore your house would be like family to her from now on.
ev.e03_fc_foundling.temple: Leave the baby at the temple
ev.e03_fc_foundling.temple.ok: The baby was carried to the temple steps and left in a basket. By evening the basket was gone; what became of the child, no one knows.
ev.e03_fc_foundling.title: A foundling at the door
ev.e03_fc_foundling.text: A few days after you were born, a baby in a torn swaddling cloth was found at your door at dawn. Your mother has milk enough for two, says the midwife - the child could be taken in as a fosterling. It could be carried to the childless neighbour who has long begged the gods for a baby. Or it could be left at the temple: someone will pick it up.
ev.e03_fc_foundling.note: In the ancient world unwanted babies were often "exposed" - left by the road, on a rubbish heap or at a temple. Many were picked up and raised as fosterlings (alumni in Rome, threptoi among the Greeks), others as slaves. In Egypt foundlings taken from rubbish heaps were named Kopreus and Kopria - "from the dung heap".
ev.e03_fc_foundling_kin.title: The foundling
ev.e03_fc_foundling_kin.text: The foundling who shared your cradle grew up at your side - closer than blood. You stole figs from the neighbours' garden together and got thrashed for it together. Now you know there is someone who would stand up for you against anyone.
ev.e03_fc_foundling_neighbor.title: The neighbour's debt
ev.e03_fc_foundling_neighbor.text: The neighbour to whom the foundling was once carried has grown old, and her adopted son is now a solid householder. At a festival she handed you a heavy purse before everyone: "Your house gave me a son - now you too should have something to start with."
ev.e03_fc_verna.nurse.ok: Your mother nursed both babies - the master's and you - and the two of you grew up in the same nursery. The mistress gave her a new tunic, and you got the master's child's old cradle.
ev.e03_fc_verna.refuse: Beg them to find another nurse
ev.e03_fc_verna.refuse.ok: Your mother threw herself at the mistress's feet, and the mistress, wincing, bought a wet nurse at the market. All the milk was yours - you grew up strong.
ev.e03_fc_verna.title: The master's milk-kin
ev.e03_fc_verna.text: You were born in your master's house - a verna, a home-born slave. In those same days the mistress gave birth to a son, and your mother is called to nurse them both. If she agrees, you and the master's child will be milk-kin - such children masters sometimes teach to read and free young. But there may not be milk enough for two.
ev.e03_fc_verna.note: The milk-siblings of a master's children - collactanei - were often raised with them, educated and freed early. The lex Aelia Sentia (AD 4) forbade freeing slaves under thirty without a "lawful cause", and jurists named milk-kinship with the master among such causes.
ev.e03_fc_verna_free.title: Freedom
ev.e03_fc_verna_free.text: The master's son, who shared your mother's breast with you, has come of age and begged one gift from his father - your freedom. Before the council he named the lawful cause: "This is my milk-{g:brother|sister}." You were touched with the rod, and walked out of the house a {g:freedman|freedwoman}.
